correctness.rationale: Choosing equality partitions and ordering their blocks by least label gives a bijection between original matrices and clarified matrices with their two partitions. Row and column duplication preserves rank: the two duplication maps each have a left inverse obtained by selecting representatives. In a full-rank factorization H=UV, the maps sending a row of U or a column of V to the corresponding row or column of H are injective. Thus pairwise distinct spanning tuples are the correct factors and each H is represented by one free GL(d,q) orbit. Subspace Möbius inversion gives (2), and the basis-extension construction realizes precisely d≤a,b≤q^d for d>0; rank zero requires a=b=1. The Stirling EGF and rank normalization follow by summing the partition bijection. Independent direct enumeration used field elimination and distinct row/column vectors for every binary matrix of sizes 2×2, 3×3, 4×4 and every ternary 2×2 matrix. All profiles matched (1); the clarified binary vectors by rank were (96,168) and (96,13608,20160) for 3×3 and 4×4. These tests are bounded; the proof, not those counts, establishes the field-general claim. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not run; the direct replay is to enumerate the q^(rm) entry arrays, bucket by row and column set sizes and elimination rank, and compare each bucket to (1).

evidence: A181230 uses two signed-Stirling sums applied to 2^(ij). For a named matrix constant on specified row/column partitions with i,j blocks, its rank equals the rank of the i×j quotient, so the rank-d count under those constraints is C_q(i,j,d)=[i choose d]_q[j choose d]_q|GL(d,q)|.

The same product-partition inversion derives H_q(a,b,d)=Σ_{i≤a,j≤b}s(a,i)s(b,j)C_q(i,j,d), with s signed Stirling numbers of the first kind. Multiplying by the two Stirling numbers of the second kind gives the joint count. The inverse sums factor; they count distinct spanning tuples, yielding the same count as (1).

value.rationale: The parameters are natural, but the proposed exact census is a mechanical application of the established unranked double Stirling inversion with q^(ij) replaced by the standard rank-d count of an i×j quotient. This works because copying rows and columns preserves rank, with no additional counting problem on a specified partition. The EGF is then the ordinary Stirling substitution and the support is the elementary dimension/cardinality bound with a basis padded by distinct vectors. The alternative factorization is a convenient expression of the determined census, but does not establish a separate substantive result that rescues this frozen finding. The failure is for scientific value as a distinct exact finding, not for false formulas or inaccessible literature.
